title: Hybrid FP8+INT4 tiled KV-cache experiments and graceful rollback plan
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Background: Continuous batching and larger context windows are increasing GPU memory pressure from KV caches. Earlier experiments focused on per-layer quantization sweeps; this ticket scopes an applied field evaluation of a hybrid tiled encoding strategy that mixes FP8 for recent keys and aggressive INT4 for colder slabs, with a per-tile residual compensation path to recover important high-fidelity vectors. Goal: measure actual quality impact across production-like workloads, quantify memory and throughput improvements, and define safe rollback/mitigation policies for canary and progressive rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Memory: demonstrate >=40% average KV cache memory reduction vs FP16 baseline for long-context workloads in our A/B cluster samples
Quality: end-to-end downstream QA F1 drop <=0.75% on internal eval set AND embedding cosine similarity >=0.994 vs FP16 baseline
Latency: p99 token latency delta <=10ms for short-turn chat (<=64 tokens) under production batching shape
Safety: automated rollback triggers in console and a documented manual rollback runbook
Observability: token-level quality telemetry, per-route regression alerts, and differential traces for requests hitting tiled INT4 vs FP8 slab
experiment_plan: Implement tiled slab encoder: split KV per-head into hot window (last N tokens) encoded in FP8 and cold slabs quantized to INT4 with per-slab scale/zero and a 1-layer residual compensation table
Add runtime flags: --kv-tile-size, --int4-threshold, --residual-tier to toggle strategy per-deployment
Create synthetic stress harness: long-context (>8k) generation, sparse retrieval+generation, and prefix-reuse chat flows using internal eval corpus
Instrument sampling: 10% of production requests for canary in a dedicated region; store dequantized vectors for offline analysis with user PII stripped
Run microbenchmarks: memory usage, throughput (tokens/sec), and latency under batch shapes observed in the logs (batch size distribution), on both A100 and H100 pools
Evaluate quality: embedding cosine, token-level mismatch, perplexity shift, and downstream QA/NER/QA F1/ROUGE where applicable
Iterate: tune tile-size, bias-correction in dequant, and residual-table size based on trade-offs found
Rollout strategy: local smoke -> dedicated canary region (10%) -> gradual weight-based rollout (10/25/50/100) with automated rollback checks per cohort
datasets: embedded-evals-v2 (512k embedding pairs for cosine baseline)
question-answering-merged-2024 (multi-domain QA eval set used across runtime experiments)
initial_findings: Prototype microbench on A100 shows 42-48% KV memory reduction with hybrid tile config (tile_size=128, hot_window=256) compared to FP16 baseline
Embedding cosine on small eval slice dropped from 0.997 to 0.995 with default int4 packing; residual-table of 256 entries recovers to 0.9965
Perplexity shift on long completion subset: +0.8% with default config; heavy degradation observed only on extremely sparse retrieval contexts without residual compensation
p99 latency increased by ~6ms in our test harness for small-turns, within target, but tail widened under simulated contention—must test with real traffic shapes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: rare high-impact regressions in safety-sensitive prompts where low-bit compression removes signal; Mitigation: keep FP8 region for last N tokens and add SLO-driven fail-open to FP16 for flagged routes
Risk: observability blind spots for cold-slab induced hallucination; Mitigation: store sampled dequantized vectors and add model-output semantic similarity checks to catch regressions quickly
Risk: GPU kernel numerical instability on certain H100 driver versions; Mitigation: pin tested CUDA/cuDNN combos and abort rollout on mismatch
Risk: increased GC/OOM in mixed deployments during rollout; Mitigation: conservative canary sizing, autoscaling buffer, and a preflight memory check in the agent
rollback_plan: Automated rollback triggers: if embedding_cosine_mean drops >0.002 vs baseline OR qa_f1_delta_percent >1.0 OR p99_token_latency_ms increases >20% for rollout cohort -> immediate traffic revert
Manual rollback steps: disable runtime flag, trigger immediate model variant fallback to FP16-armed KV codepath, purge cache entries if necessary and warm FP16 path
Post-rollback audit: capture last 10k canary requests, run offline evaluation to triage failure root cause and publish incident note
instrumentation_and_observability: Add per-request tag: kv_tile_strategy=hybrid_fp8_int4 and tile_metadata on traces
Sample dequantized KV vectors for offline SNR analysis (1/1,000 requests), PII removal applied
Add differential dashboards: cohort vs baseline for metrics list and per-route alerting thresholds
Trace-level debug mode to log token-level logits difference for failed regression alerts
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for quantize/dequantize invariants and residual-table lookup correctness
Integration tests exercising multi-GPU KV shard handoff with tiled encoding enabled
Fuzz tests with pathological sequences (repeated tokens, adversarial prompts) to surface numerical edge cases
End-to-end canary traffic validation using mirrored requests and golden-response comparison harness
